chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
He said: 'Do not eat the jarith, nor the marmahiya, nor the tafi', nor the tihal, for it is the house of blood and the morsel of the Shaytan.'

key_terms.اَلْجِرِّيثُ: A specific type of fish, often identified as the sturgeon or a similar large fish.
key_terms.اَلْمَارْمَاهِيُّ: A specific type of fish, often identified as the carp or a similar freshwater fish.
key_terms.بَيْتُ الدَّمِ: The house of blood, a metaphorical description indicating high blood content or bloodiness.
key_terms.طَافِيًا: Floating (fish), referring to fish that float on the surface of the water.
key_terms.طِحَالًا: A type of fish, often identified as the catfish or a similar bottom-dwelling fish.
key_terms.مُضْغَةُ اَلشَّيْطَانِ: The morsel of the Shaytan, a metaphorical description indicating spiritual or physical impurity.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific types of fish mentioned as being 'the house of blood' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines specific prohibitions regarding the consumption of certain aquatic creatures, notably the 'Jirith' and 'Marmahi,' characterizing them as 'houses of blood' and the 'morsel of the Shaytan.' In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of *istihya* (shyness/modesty) and physical impurity (*khabath*), linking their blood-heavy nature to spiritual detestation. The description serves as a mnemonic for distinguishing between pure (*tayyib*) and impure (*khabith*) marine life in dietary laws.
